blocks.name: By eye
blocks.note: No instrument: ranges by eye, about 20% of the range (fire-control-research.md §3.1). A director without a rangefinder, or one whose instrument isn't read.

blocks.name: Barr & Stroud FA (O1)
blocks.note: Early coincidence, c.1895-1906: the FA2 and FA3 4.5 ft (1.37 m) at ×24, the Japanese ships' at Tsushima and Oslyabya's (§3.3; early-hit-rates.md). O1: 14″, rigid to 2 m, ×20 at a full image (designer §2.5). Unstabilised, 2 readings a minute (§3.5).

blocks.name: Barr & Stroud FQ/FT (O2)
blocks.note: Mature coincidence, c.1906-1925: the FQ2 9 ft (2.74 m) and FT24 15 ft (4.57 m) at ×28 (§3.3). O2: 12″, rigid to 4 m (designer §2.5). Unstabilised, 2 readings a minute (§3.5).

blocks.name: Barr & Stroud FQ/FT on the Argo mounting
blocks.note: The O2 instruments on Pollen's gyro-stabilised mounting: range-taking about fivefold, 8 readings a minute (§3.5).

blocks.name: Zeiss stereo (WWI)
blocks.note: The German 3 m stereo of 1914-18 at ×23: Lienau's ±65 m at 10 km and 165 m at 16 km give 10″ (§3.3). Rigid base as O2's [EST]; unstabilised, 2 readings a minute (§3.5). Stereo's haze and contrast advantages are the sensors' (F5).

blocks.name: Stereo, long base (O3)
blocks.note: Interwar stereo and long bases (Zeiss, interwar B&S), c.1925-40: O3, 12″, rigid to 5 m (designer §2.5). 4 readings a minute (§3.5's WWII director 4-6).

blocks.name: Stereo, long base (O3, ×23)
blocks.note: O3 at ×23: Bismarck's 10.5 m stereo (§3.3, its magnification [INFERRED]).

blocks.name: Stereo, long base (O3, ×25)
blocks.note: O3 at ×25: the Japanese plot's preset (fire_control_ref.py LEVELS).

blocks.name: Coated, stabilised (O4)
blocks.note: USN 1943: coated, gyro-stabilised, rigid to 6 m (designer §2.5); the Mk 48 26.5 ft at ×25 (§3.3); 6 readings a minute (§3.5).

blocks.name: Auto-track ranging (radar stand-in)
blocks.note: O4's instruments read as an auto-tracking radar's range: 60 a minute (§3.5). Stands in for the radar block until the radar pass.

blocks.name: Digital ranging (radar and laser stand-in)
blocks.note: O4's instruments read as the 1970s' radar and laser: 30 a minute (fire_control_ref.py LEVELS 8). Stands in for the radar block.

blocks.name: Judgement
blocks.note: A sailor's eye and head: the range guessed, the target's course and speed guessed from her look and led by it, looked at again each minute, never a rate learnt (F2: the worst computer there is). The eye's guess and the tables' corrections as the hand plot's: the same eye, the same tables (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL3).

blocks.name: Hand plot
blocks.note: Ranges, by rangefinder or by eye, plotted by hand, no machine (levels 0 and 1: the Tsushima era; designer C0). Its rates are the plot's trend alone (no Dumaresq to make them from her course and speed: "range rate was ignored, or guessed by rule of thumb"), and the range passed at each plot stays on the sights until the next (no clock to run it on): manual-gunnery-research.md §3.2, computing.md §2 (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL4). The reference's level 0 had an "eye and hand plot" of its own, slower and with worse guesses and corrections for no difference in the plot: gone (FL3).

blocks.name: Dumaresq and Vickers clock
blocks.note: The Dumaresq's rates run on by the Vickers range clock (1906): constant rates only, the roller slipping on a change (computing.md §3; level 2, designer C1).

blocks.name: German range clock (EU-Anzeiger)
blocks.note: The German WWI range-rate indicator and clock without the plot, the cruisers' (computing.md §3): no specifications found; taken as the Dumaresq and Vickers clock's [EST].

blocks.name: Dreyer table Mk I
blocks.note: The first Dreyer table's range and bearing plots and clock (1911), her course set on it by handwheel: the Mk III's numbers without helm-free, so own ship's turns are re-learnt (ship-motion/own-motion-inputs.md §2: the 1918 handbook has the Mk I's course by "handwheel input", the Mk I* on "automatic", the Mk II "automatic ?"; docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL5).

blocks.name: Dreyer table Mk III-V
blocks.note: The Dreyer table from the Mk I* (1912-22; named for the Mk III, the marks most ships had), helm-free by the gyro: a rate clock limited to ±1,200 yd/min and ±15°/min, its bearing plot the weak point (computing.md §3; level 3, designer C2). Crew 7-8 at the table, up to 30 in the station. Its first guess at her course and speed the Dumaresq's in it, from the same eye (FL5).

blocks.name: German clock and plot (EU-Anzeiger, C12)
blocks.note: The German WWI range-rate clock and plot (computing.md §3). No specifications found; taken as the Dreyer Mk III's, helm-free by the gyro [EST], the two navies' 1916 machines doing the same job.

blocks.name: Argo clock Mk IV
blocks.note: Pollen's true-course plotter and variable-speed clock (1912-13): follows a changing range rate, gyro-corrected; about six in RN service at Jutland (computing.md §3; fire_control_ref.py level 3b). Mass and crew [EST]. Its first guess at her course and speed the Dumaresq's, from the same eye behind the same ×28 (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL11).

blocks.name: Admiralty Fire Control Table
blocks.note: The AFCT Mk I-X (1927-45): clock and MPI plot, helm-free, a straight-course target (computing.md §3; level 4, designer C3). Its first guess at her course and speed the Dumaresq's, from the same eye (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL6).

blocks.name: Admiralty Fire Control Clock
blocks.note: The AFCC, the AFCT without its plot, for destroyers and secondaries (computing.md §3; Haida's Mk III limited to 16,000 yd): the table's numbers [EST]; mass and crew [EST].

blocks.name: Admiralty Fire Control Table, turn setting
blocks.note: The AFCT with a hand-set enemy rate of turn: a turn filter whose rate adapts slowly (level 4t; [UNCERTAIN] in the research, a computer option anyone may fit, decision 5).

blocks.name: German Rechenstelle (1930s)
blocks.note: The German computing rooms of the 1930s, fore and aft under armour (computing.md §3): no specifications found; the research's table puts them with the AFCT, whose numbers they take [EST].

blocks.name: Type 92 Shagekiban
blocks.note: The Japanese Type 92 (1932) with its Sokutekiban: rates from a range-rate plot, deflection by hand, no gyro horizon; rates rebuilt after a manoeuvre (computing.md §3; level 4j). Crew 7 + 8; mass [EST]. Own course followed by hand from the gyro's pointer ("Follow up compass course as received from the gyrocompass": ship-motion/own-motion-inputs.md §2), 0.5 s behind [EST: a man following a pointer, the user]; own speed set by crank, 20 s [EST]. Its first guess at her course and speed the Dumaresq's, from the same eye (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL11).

blocks.name: Ford Mk 8 rangekeeper
blocks.note: The Ford Mk 8 with the stable vertical (1941-42): continuous, helm-free, tilt, wind and drift corrected; one operator (computing.md §3; level 5, designer C4). Its first guess at her course and speed the Dumaresq's, from the same eye (docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL7).

blocks.name: Ford Mk 8 rangekeeper, radar ranging (stand-in)
blocks.note: The Mk 8 fed by radar spotting (level 6): its shorter latency is the radar's, standing in until the radar pass.

blocks.name: Curved-course analog computer (1950s)
blocks.note: The 1950s analog with a curved-course (acceleration) predictor, the Mk 56/68 systems' (level 7, designer C5; fire_control_ref.py level 7; Sperry's target course predictor, filed 1954: fire-control-research.md §5.6). Not the Ford Mk 1A, the WWII Mk 37's computer, which took a straight-line target and had the "target just turned" button (NavPers Ch. 19-F; docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL9). The acceleration it allows, 0.25 m/s² 1σ, is a capital ship's in a hard turn, her speed times her rate of turn (25 kn at 1°/s about 0.22, the reference's own figure; QE at 18 kn with 15° of helm 0.14).

blocks.name: Digital turn filter (Mk 86, WM-25)
blocks.note: The 1970s digital systems with a turn-following filter (level 8, designer C6; the filter [INFERRED]). How fast it lets her rate of turn change, 2e-5 rad²/s³, is a capital ship's helm: the rate hard over makes, squared, over the time her yaw takes to answer (QE at 18 kn: 1.3°/s over Nomoto's 28 s, 1.9e-5; the reference's 5e-7 learnt a turn and shed it so slowly it fell behind the Mk 8 on a zigzag: docs/battle/fc-ladder-check.md FL10). Its speed noise the same way, the way she loses in a hard turn: a quarter of her speed in a minute, 0.1 (F2; the reference's 0.05²).

blocks.name: Open sights
blocks.note: Each gun laid by its layer over open sights, fired on the roll (the open sight's 4′ on a steady platform: 1.15 mil; the roll his timing's): before continuous aim, to the late 1890s (level 0).

blocks.name: Telescopic sights, fired on the roll
blocks.note: Each gun by its own telescope, fired as the roll brings the sight on (the telescope's 1.2′: 0.35 mil; the roll his timing's): heavy guns until power laying, continuous aim working only to about 9.2″ (fire-control-research.md §6).

blocks.name: Early telescopic sights
blocks.note: Each gun by its own early telescope, continuous aim (the early telescope's 2.5′: 0.73 mil; M0): the medium guns of 1899-1905, the Tsushima era (level 1).

blocks.name: Telescopic sights
blocks.note: Each gun by a good telescope, continuous aim (the telescope's 1.2′: 0.35 mil), no director (level 2).

blocks.name: Director, follow the pointer
blocks.note: Director firing: the guns laid and fired from the director, the turrets following its pointers (M1, 1912-16; level 3; the reference's 1 mil less its roll: 0.5).

blocks.name: Director, follow the pointer (no RPC)
blocks.note: Director firing without remote power control, the Japanese 1930s (no RPC on Yamato, computing.md §3): the Japanese plot's preset numbers (the reference's 1 mil less its roll: 0.5).

blocks.name: Director, power drive
blocks.note: Director firing with power training and elevation (M2, interwar; level 4; the reference's 0.8 mil less its roll: 0.4).

blocks.name: Stable vertical, remote power control
blocks.note: A stable vertical and gyro firing, the mounts under remote power control (M3, 1941-45; levels 5-6).

blocks.name: Stable vertical, power servo
blocks.note: The 1950s' servos (fire_control_ref.py level 7), between M3 and M4.

blocks.name: Digital servo
blocks.note: Digital servos (M4, 1970s; level 8).

presets.name: eyeball
presets.note: Level 0, c.1890: ranges by eye, each gun laid by its own layer.

presets.name: director
presets.note: Level 3, 1916: the Dreyer table and director firing.

presets.name: table
presets.note: Level 4, the 1930s: the interwar central table.

presets.name: radar-spotting
presets.note: Level 6, 1945: radar spotting (its radar a stand-in until the radar pass).

presets.name: judgement
presets.note: A sailor's judgement: the worst computer, for comparison (F2).

presets.name: argo
fit: Barr & Stroud FQ/FT on the Argo mounting

presets.name: table-turn
presets.note: The AFCT with its turn setting (level 4t, decision 5).
fit: Admiralty Fire Control Table, turn setting
